newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel vows to shun envoys who visit PLO building.
newsitem.headline: Israel vows to shun envoys who visit PLO building.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed on Tuesday not to receive European foreign ministers should they visit PLO headquarters in Jerusalem.
"We informed the European foreign ministers that if they visit Orient House, we will not receive them," a parliamentary official quoted Netanyahu as telling a closed-door committee.

Orient House, in Arab East Jerusalem, is a symbol of the PLO's nationalist aspirations and its desire to make East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, the capital of a future state.
Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring said this month the European "troika" of ministers from Ireland, Netherlands and Italy wanted to go to Orient House but did not say they would go through with it.

Israel regards both halves of the city as its eternal capital and Netanyahu, head of the right-wing Likud party which came to power in June, insists Israel-PLO peace deals prohibit Palestinian diplomacy at the building in Jerusalem.
A handful of lawmakers on an Israeli parliamentary committee visited Orient House last week in defiance of government policy.
